questions.q: What application-architecture decision does LTV Global make, and why?
options: A separate org per region, because regions have different legal requirements
A single, global Salesforce org, because the target-state vision commits to a unified customer view no multi-org estate can deliver natively
A separate org per business unit, to maximize customization freedom
No Salesforce org at all, relying entirely on the existing legacy systems
questions.explain: LTV Global chooses a single global org because the vision's unified-customer-view commitment cannot be satisfied natively by multiple orgs, since no native Salesforce report can span two separate orgs.

questions.q: What real cost does this lesson say the single-org decision accepts?
options: Duplicated master data across every business unit
No native cross-org reporting capability whatsoever
Shared governor limits and shared platform risk, since a bad customization in one business unit affects all of them
The inability to ever support more than one business unit
questions.explain: A single org concentrates governor-limit pressure and customization risk in one shared platform — a real cost the lesson names explicitly, in contrast to multi-org's costs of duplicated master data and no native cross-org reporting.

questions.q: Which Salesforce Cloud does this lesson map to the Parts & Aftermarket Distribution business unit, given its role as the highest-volume unit?
options: Primarily Experience Cloud, for dealer self-service ordering
Primarily Marketing Cloud
Primarily CRM Analytics only, with no transactional objects
Primarily Field Service Management with no portal component
questions.explain: Parts & Aftermarket Distribution maps primarily to Experience Cloud for dealer self-service parts ordering, backed by the custom Parts Order object, which the lesson calls the highest-volume object in the design.

questions.q: How should an architect respond to the claim that EMEA needs its own separate Salesforce org specifically because of GDPR?
options: Agree immediately and split EMEA into its own org

Explain that GDPR compliance does not by itself require a separate org, and that the single-org decision instead relies on the security design and nonfunctional requirements to guarantee compliant handling of EMEA personal data
State that GDPR does not apply to Salesforce implementations
Recommend moving all EMEA data into LedgerPoint instead
questions.explain: The lesson's Lab specifically frames this: GDPR compliance is handled through the security/sharing design and nonfunctional requirements, not by defaulting to a separate org, which would undercut the vision's unified-customer-view commitment.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the single-org vs. multi-org decision is likely to be probed directly by the Architecture Review Board in Chapter 6?
options: Because it is a trivial, easily reversible decision
Because it is foundational and hard to reverse after build begins, making it exactly the kind of decision a board tests
Because the ARB only ever asks about org strategy and nothing else
Because Salesforce requires ARB approval specifically for org-count decisions
questions.explain: The lesson states that foundational, hard-to-reverse decisions like org strategy are exactly what an Architecture Review Board probes, which is why LTV Global's architect needs a clear, honest justification ready.
